examples.en: The army is stationed near the border.

examples.ko: 그 부대는 작년부터 이 도시에 주둔했어요.
examples.en: That unit has been stationed in this city since last year.
The soldiers will be stationed in the mountains.

examples.ko: 마을에 주둔하는 군인들이 시장에서 장을 봐요.
examples.en: The soldiers stationed in the village shop at the market.

examples.ko: 부대는 겨울 동안 여기에 주둔하고 있어요.
examples.en: The unit is stationed here for the winter.
People were worried because foreign troops were stationed there.

explain: 주어는 거의 군대나 부대예요. 장소 뒤에는 '에'를 붙여서 '국경에 주둔하다'라고 해요. 사람이 잠시 머무는 일에는 '머무르다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The unit is stationed at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 어느 곳에 머물러 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the current state of being stationed.

phrases.example: 그 나라에는 외국 군대가 주둔하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Foreign troops are stationed in that country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 군대가 계속 머무르는 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news for troops staying on an ongoing basis.

phrases.en: The army came to be stationed in this area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주둔이 정해졌다는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses that the stationing has been decided or has come about.

explain_en: The subject is almost always an army or a unit. Put 에 after the place, as in '국경에 주둔하다'. For a person staying somewhere briefly, use 머무르다.

examples.en: The soldiers advanced toward the enemy camp.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 결승전을 향해 진격하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is charging toward the final.
The army kept advancing even in the fog.
The general ordered them to advance at dawn.
The unit that was advancing west stopped.
The commander said he would advance at daybreak.

explain: 진격하다는 군대가 적을 향해 용감하게 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. 스포츠나 게임 이야기에서 기세 좋게 이기며 올라가는 것을 말할 때도 비유로 써요. 일상에서 그냥 앞으로 가는 것은 '나아가다', '가다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The enemy advanced toward the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하는 쪽을 향해 다가올 때 '-아/어 오다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 오다' shows the advance is coming toward the speaker.

phrases.en: The general said, "Let's advance."
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 나아가자는 말을 전할 때 '-자고 하다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-자고 하다' reports a suggestion or call to advance together.

phrases.en: We keep moving forward toward our goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대가 아니어도 쓸 수 있는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word that doesn't need a military setting.

explain_en: It describes an army moving boldly toward the enemy. In sports or game talk, it can be used figuratively for winning and moving up with momentum. For ordinary moving forward in daily life, use 나아가다 or 가다.

t90.ax: Our team is charging toward the final.

examples.ko: 전쟁이 길어지자 징집 대상 나이가 낮아졌어요.
examples.en: As the war dragged on, the age of those subject to conscription was lowered.

examples.ko: 그는 갑작스러운 징집 통보를 받고 학교를 떠났어요.
examples.en: He received a sudden conscription notice and left school.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 일제강점기의 강제 징집에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about forced conscription during the Japanese colonial period.

examples.ko: 징집을 피하려고 외국으로 떠난 사람들이 있었어요.
examples.en: There were people who left for other countries to avoid being drafted.

examples.ko: 징집 통지서가 나오기 전까지 가족은 아무것도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: The family knew nothing until the draft notice arrived.
A debate broke out over the draft age.

explain: 나라나 군대가 사람들을 군인으로 불러 모으는 일이에요. 비슷한 '징병'과 함께 나오는 일이 많고, 개인이 군대에 들어가는 일은 '입대'라고 해요.

phrases.en: People subject to conscription must take a physical exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에 불려 갈 사람을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to people who may be called up for the military.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 아직도 징집 제도를 유지하고 있어요.
phrases.en: That country still keeps its conscription system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라가 사람들을 군인으로 불러 모으는 제도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the system by which a country calls people into the military.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 징병이 법으로 정해져 있어요.
phrases.en: Conscription is stipulated by law in that country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '징집'과 비슷하고 둘이 함께 나오는 일이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 징집, and the two often appear together.

explain_en: It refers to a state or army calling people up to serve as soldiers. It often appears together with the similar word '징병', and an individual joining the military is called '입대'.

examples.en: Our school marks its 100th anniversary this year.
We get a day off on the company's founding anniversary.

examples.ko: 창립 멤버는 지금도 같이 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: The founding members still work together.

examples.ko: 동아리 창립 모임이 내일 저녁에 있어요.
examples.en: The club's founding meeting is tomorrow evening.
They held a big party to celebrate the founding.
The founding spirit of this shop is honesty.

explain: '설립'은 법적으로 기관을 세우는 절차에 가깝고, '창립'은 단체나 회사가 처음 시작된 순간과 그 뜻을 기념할 때 많이 써요. 혼자 사업을 시작하면 '창업'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: We get a day off on the company's founding anniversary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단체가 처음 시작된 날을 기념하는 날이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The day that marks when an organization was first founded.

phrases.en: He is a founding member of this club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단체를 처음 만들 때부터 함께한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who was there from the very start of the group.

phrases.en: My older brother started a cafe last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자 사업을 시작할 때는 '창립'이 아니라 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 창립 when starting a business on your own.

explain_en: 설립 leans toward the legal act of setting up an institution, while 창립 is often used for the moment a group or company began and its meaning, as in anniversaries. Starting a business on your own is 창업.

t90.ax: The founding members still work together.

examples.en: The new CEO promised change in the inaugural speech.
I listened to the president's inaugural address on the radio.
The principal's inaugural speech was short but moving.

examples.ko: 취임사에 쓸 내용을 며칠째 고민하고 있어요.
examples.en: I've been thinking for days about what to put in my inaugural speech.

examples.ko: 신임 선생님이 첫날 간단한 취임사를 하셨어요.
examples.en: The new teacher gave a brief inaugural speech on the first day.
The inaugural speech was long, so people got bored.

explain: 새로 일을 맡은 사람이 하는 인사 연설이에요. '취임사를 하다/발표하다'로 쓰고, 떠나는 사람이 하는 말은 '이임사', 물러나는 사람이 하는 말은 '퇴임사'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 새 시장이 시청 앞에서 취임사를 했어요.
phrases.en: The new mayor gave an inaugural address in front of city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연설을 직접 한다는 행동을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pairing for actually delivering the speech.

phrases.en: The new principal delivered the inaugural address.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'보다 공식적이고 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than 하다 and common in news.

phrases.example: 취임 연설에서 대표가 감사 인사를 전했어요.
phrases.en: In his inaugural speech, the CEO expressed his thanks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻을 '연설'로 풀어 쓴 말이라 조금 더 이해하기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same idea spelled out with 연설, slightly easier to grasp.

explain_en: It is the greeting speech given by someone taking on a new post. It is used as '취임사를 하다/발표하다', while the speech of a person leaving a post is '이임사' and that of one retiring is '퇴임사'.

examples.ko: 판결문에는 재판부가 그렇게 판단한 이유가 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The written judgment explains why the court decided that way.

examples.ko: 판결문을 읽어 보니 내용이 생각보다 복잡했어요.
examples.en: When I read the written judgment, it was more complicated than I expected.
When the written judgment comes out, the news reports it right away.

examples.ko: 이 판결문은 인터넷에서 누구나 찾아볼 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can anyone look up this written judgment online?
The lawyer checked part of the written judgment again.
It's fine to read only the summary of the judgment first.

explain: '판결'은 재판의 결론이고, '판결문'은 그 결론과 이유를 적은 문서예요. '판결이 나다, 판결을 내리다'처럼 말하고, 문서는 '판결문을 읽다, 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 뉴스에서 '판결문에 따르면'이라는 표현이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The reporter read the written judgment and wrote an article.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문서를 직접 읽는다는 뜻으로 '판결문'과 자주 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Reading the document itself; a verb often paired with 판결문.

phrases.en: According to the judgment, the defendant is not liable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 근거를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news to cite the source.

phrases.example: 판결문이 공개돼서 누구나 내용을 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: The judgment has been made public, so anyone can see it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문서가 알려졌다는 뜻의 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive expression meaning the document was released.

explain_en: '판결' is the court's conclusion, while '판결문' is the document that records the conclusion and the reasons. You say '판결이 나다' or '판결을 내리다' for the decision, and '판결문을 읽다' or '쓰다' for the document. The phrase '판결문에 따르면' (according to the judgment) is common in the news.

en: to judge; to rule on a case; to give a verdict

examples.en: The court ruled on the case today.
The judge rules based on the evidence.

examples.ko: 판결할 때는 모든 사실을 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to check all the facts when you pass judgment.

examples.ko: 재판부가 무죄로 판결하면 피고는 바로 풀려나요.
examples.en: If the court rules not guilty, the defendant is released right away.
This issue is hard to settle in court.

examples.ko: 법원이 어떻게 판결할지 모두 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is waiting to see how the court will rule.

explain: 판결하다는 재판에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. 일상에서 무언가를 정할 때는 '결정하다'나 '정하다'를 써요. 보통 '판결을 내리다'처럼 명사와 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: The judge gave a verdict today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '판결하다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This pairing is more common than '판결하다'.

phrases.en: The court ruled that the person was guilty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판의 결과를 '-라고'로 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-라고' to report the result of a trial.

phrases.en: The verdict for that trial comes out tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판의 결과가 정해져 나온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means the result of a trial is announced.

explain_en: This is a courtroom word and rarely appears in everyday talk. For ordinary decisions Koreans say '결정하다' or '정하다'. It is usually paired with the noun, as in '판결을 내리다'.

dis.h: decide a case as a judge
gh: everyday word for choosing or fixing something
settle for good; make final and confirmed

p.n: 판결하다 is only for judges ruling on a case, so a general verb sounds wrong here.

t90.ax: The court ruled on the case today.

examples.en: The lawmakers vote on the bill this afternoon.
Opinions were divided, so we decided to put it to a vote.

examples.ko: 반장을 뽑을 때 손을 들어 표결했어요.
examples.en: When choosing the class president, we voted by raising hands.
To hold a vote, you first have to decide the agenda item.

examples.ko: 이 안건은 다음 주에 표결할 예정이에요.
examples.en: This item is scheduled to be voted on next week.
Sometimes they decide by applause without voting.

explain: '투표하다'는 선거나 여럿이 고를 때 널리 쓰고, '표결하다'는 회의나 국회에서 안건을 찬성과 반대로 결정할 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '표결에 부치다', '표결 처리'처럼 명사 '표결'로도 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 국회는 그 법안을 표결에 부치기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The National Assembly decided to put the bill to a vote.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안건을 투표로 결정하게 올린다는 뜻으로, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to bring a matter up for a vote. Common in the news.

phrases.en: That item was decided by a vote.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의에서 투표로 결정이 났을 때 쓰는 뉴스 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news expression used when a meeting settles something by voting.

phrases.en: Opinions differ, so we are holding a vote today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '표결'에 '하다'를 붙여서 쉽게 말하는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say it by attaching 하다 to the noun 표결.

explain_en: '투표하다' is used widely for elections or any group choice, while '표결하다' is for deciding an agenda item by yes or no votes in a meeting or the National Assembly. In the news the noun '표결' is also common, as in '표결에 부치다' and '표결 처리'.

t90.ax: The lawmakers vote on the bill this afternoon.

examples.en: The navy fleet entered the port.
In the movie, the space fleet protected the Earth.

examples.ko: 이순신 장군의 함대는 바다에서 크게 이겼어요.
examples.en: General Yi Sun-sin's fleet won a great victory at sea.

examples.ko: 배 열 척으로 이루어진 함대를 만들었어요.
examples.en: They built a fleet made up of ten ships.
I saw a model of an old fleet at the museum.
The fleet commander gave the order to set sail.

explain: 역사 이야기나 전쟁·우주 영화에서 자주 나와요. 배가 많이 모여 있어도 군함이 아니면 보통 '선단'이라고 해요. '우주 함대'처럼 상상 속 이야기에도 써요.

phrases.en: The enemy fleet appeared on the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전쟁 이야기에서 상대편 군함 무리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in war stories for the opposing side's group of warships.

phrases.en: The fleet departs tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함대'를 주어로 해서 움직임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '함대' as the subject to describe its movement.

phrases.en: A fleet of fishing boats went out to sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군함이 아닌 배가 모여 있을 때는 '선단'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '선단' for a group of ships that are not warships.

explain_en: It comes up often in history and in war or space movies. A group of many ships that are not warships is usually called '선단'. It is also used in imagined stories, as in '우주 함대'.

examples.ko: 백제 금동 대향로는 국립부여박물관에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the Baekje Gilt-bronze Incense Burner at the National Buyeo Museum.

examples.ko: 이 금동 불상은 천 년이 넘었어요.
examples.en: This gilt-bronze Buddha statue is over a thousand years old.

examples.ko: 금동으로 만든 작은 종이 전시돼 있어요.
examples.en: A small bell made of gilt bronze is on display.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 금동 관을 봤는데 정말 화려했어요.
examples.en: I saw a gilt-bronze crown at the museum, and it was really splendid.

examples.ko: 이 박물관에는 금동 유물이 아주 많아요.
examples.en: This museum has many gilt-bronze artifacts.

examples.ko: 금동 장식이 달린 상자를 선물로 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a box with gilt-bronze decorations as a gift.

explain: 주로 박물관과 문화재 설명에서 '금동 불상', '금동 대향로'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙어서 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않지만 한국 역사나 여행 이야기에서는 꼭 만나요.

phrases.en: I saw a small gilt bronze Buddha statue at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: '금동' 뒤에 가장 자주 붙는 짝말이고, 문화재 설명에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word to follow 금동, often seen in descriptions of cultural properties.

phrases.en: An old gilt bronze crown was found in the tomb.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛 무덤에서 나온 왕관을 말할 때 쓰는 역사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A history term for a crown found in an old tomb.

phrases.example: 그 문에는 금동 장식이 붙어 있어요.
phrases.en: That door has gilt bronze decorations on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건에 붙은 금동 꾸밈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for gilt bronze ornaments attached to an object.

explain_en: It mostly appears in museum and cultural-heritage explanations, placed before another noun, as in '금동 불상' or '금동 대향로'. You rarely use it in everyday talk, but you will meet it when reading about Korean history or travel.

examples.ko: 온몸을 두꺼운 옷으로 동여매서 걷기도 힘들어요.
examples.en: I'm bundled up in thick clothes from head to toe, so it's hard even to walk.
I wrapped the injured arm tightly with cloth.

examples.ko: 짐이 흩어지지 않게 끈으로 동여매 주세요.
examples.en: Please tie the luggage with a strap so it doesn't come apart.
I tied a towel around my head and started cleaning.

examples.ko: 허리를 띠로 동여매니까 옷이 덜 흘러내려요.
examples.en: Since I tied a belt around my waist, the clothes slip down less.

examples.ko: 책 묶음은 끈으로 동여매면 들고 다니기 편해요.
examples.en: If you bind a bundle of books with a string, it's easy to carry.

explain: '묶다'보다 여러 번 감아서 단단히 매는 느낌이 있어요. 몸이나 상처, 짐처럼 꽉 감싸 고정하는 것에 잘 어울려요. 주로 '~을 ~으로 동여매다'의 모양으로 써요.

phrases.en: I tied a towel around my head and started cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천이나 끈으로 머리를 단단히 감쌀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when wrapping a cloth or cord tightly around the head.
phrases.en_equiv: to tie a towel around one's head

phrases.en: I tied the moving boxes tightly with a rope and loaded them in the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈으로 여러 번 감아 짐을 꽉 묶을 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits tying luggage tightly by winding rope around it several times.
phrases.en_equiv: to bind luggage with a rope

phrases.en: I wrapped the cut on my finger tightly with a bandage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳을 감싸서 고정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when wrapping an injury to hold it in place.
phrases.en_equiv: to bind a wound with a bandage

explain_en: It feels firmer than '묶다', as if you wind something around several times and tie it tightly. It suits fixing things snugly, like a body, a wound or luggage. It is mostly used in the pattern '~을 ~으로 동여매다'.

t90.ax: I wrapped the injured arm tightly with cloth.

examples.en: This bowl is concave in the middle.
The inside of a spoon is shaped hollow.
I put the soup in a dished plate.
The ground is dented, so water collected.
The belly button is a dented part of the body.
If a mirror is concave, your face looks bigger.

explain: 가운데가 안으로 들어간 모양을 말하고, 반대로 가운데가 볼록 나온 모양은 '볼록하다'예요. 비슷한 말로 '움푹하다'는 더 깊게 푹 들어갔을 때 써요. 수학·과학에서 '오목 렌즈'로도 나와요.

phrases.en: I put soup in a concave bowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 '오목한'으로 바꿔요.
phrases.nuance_en: Change to 오목한 to describe a noun.

phrases.en: This plate isn't concave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가운데가 안으로 들어가지 않았다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the middle doesn't curve inward.

phrases.en: The ground is sunken, so water collected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오목하다보다 더 깊이 들어갔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a deeper dent than 오목하다.

explain_en: It describes a shape with the center curved inward; the opposite, bulging outward, is 볼록하다. 움푹하다 is similar but deeper. In science it appears as 오목 렌즈 (concave lens).

examples.en: People in prehistoric times lived in pit dwellings.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 움집을 실제 크기로 만들어 놓은 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum I saw a life-size pit dwelling.

examples.ko: 움집 가운데에는 불을 피우는 자리가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a spot for a fire in the middle of the pit dwelling.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 움집의 구조를 그림으로 그렸어요.
examples.en: In history class we drew the structure of a pit dwelling.

examples.ko: 아이들이 체험 학습에서 움집 안에 들어가 봤어요.
examples.en: The kids went inside a pit dwelling on the field trip.

examples.ko: 이 근처에서 신석기 시대 움집 터가 발견됐어요.
examples.en: The site of a Neolithic pit dwelling was found near here.

explain: 주로 선사 시대 집을 이야기할 때 역사 수업이나 박물관에서 나오는 말이에요. 요즘 집을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요. '초가집'은 짚으로 지붕을 얹은 지상의 집을 떠올리게 해서 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: People dug into the ground and built pit dwellings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 사람들이 집을 만드는 모습을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing how ancient people built homes.

phrases.en: The site of a pit dwelling was found at the excavation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이 있던 자리를 말하고 역사 설명에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to where a house once stood; common in history explanations.

phrases.en: Pit dwelling remains were found by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 움집이 남긴 흔적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to remains left by ancient pit dwellings.

explain_en: This word mostly comes up in history class or museums when talking about prehistoric houses. You would not use it for houses today. '초가집' brings to mind a thatched house built above ground, so the image is different.

en: to be biggish; to be rather big

examples.en: I bought a nice big bag.
The apple is big, so even one makes me full.
If the writing is big, it's easy to read.
A child with big eyes is smiling.
The rooms in this house are spacious and bright.
I put in potatoes cut into big pieces.

explain: '크다'보다 보기 좋고 시원하게 큰 느낌이 있어요. '큼직하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 가방, 눈, 글씨, 채소 조각처럼 눈에 보이는 것에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: It's a big bag, so all my stuff fits.
phrases.nuance_ko: '큼지막하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 더 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 큼지막하다 and more commonly used.

phrases.en: I wrote in big letters for my grandmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form modifies a noun that follows.

phrases.en: This potato is really big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 문장을 끝낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to end a sentence in polite style.

explain_en: It feels more pleasantly and satisfyingly big than plain '크다'. It is used almost the same as '큼직하다'. It fits visible things such as bags, eyes, handwriting and chunks of vegetables.
